photos.question: The nurse is preparing insulin glargine for a client with diabetes. Which statement about this insulin is correct?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #245!

💉 Can you mix insulin glargine with other insulins in the same syringe?

This is a HIGH-YIELD pharmacology question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: B — It Should Not Be Mixed with Other Insulins

🧠 Rationale: Insulin glargine is a long-acting basal insulin.

Mixing it with other insulins can change how it is absorbed and how well it works.

It has no real peak and is given subcutaneously, never IV.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Insulin Glargine

💊 Drug Class: Long-acting insulin

❤️ Primary Use: Steady 24 hour basal blood glucose control

⚠️ Watch For:

🔹 Hypoglycemia: shaky, sweaty, confused

🔹 Injection site reactions

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Never mix in the same syringe

✅ Give once daily at the same time

✅ Give subcutaneously only

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Glargine goes it alone: no peak, no mixing, no IV!

photos.question: A client is prescribed sublingual nitroglycerin for chest pain. Which instruction should the nurse include?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #246!

❤️ Chest pain and a nitro tablet. When does your client need to call 911?

This is a HIGH-YIELD cardiac question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: C — Call 911 if Pain Is Not Better 5 Minutes After One Dose

🧠 Rationale: Chest pain that does not improve 5 minutes after the first dose may be a heart attack.

Calling 911 early saves heart muscle.

The client may take 1 tablet every 5 minutes, up to 3 doses, as prescribed.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Sublingual Nitroglycerin

💊 Drug Class: Nitrate (vasodilator)

❤️ Primary Use: Relief of angina chest pain

⚠️ Side Effects:

🔹 Headache

🔹 Low blood pressure and dizziness

🔹 Flushing

🚨 Patient Teaching:

✅ Sit down before taking it

✅ Let it dissolve under the tongue

✅ Keep in the original dark glass bottle

✅ Avoid sildenafil and similar drugs

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

1 tab, 5 minutes, no relief? Call 911!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

photos.question: A client with a T4 spinal cord injury has a pounding headache, BP 190/104 mmHg and flushing above the injury. What should the nurse do first?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #247!

🧠 Pounding headache and sky-high BP in a spinal cord injury client. What is your FIRST move?

This is a HIGH-YIELD neuro question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: A — Sit the Client Upright

🧠 Rationale: These are signs of autonomic dysreflexia, a medical emergency.

Sitting upright and lowering the legs helps lower blood pressure fast.

Next, find and remove the trigger. A full bladder is the most common cause.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Autonomic Dysreflexia

🧠 Who Is at Risk: Spinal cord injury at T6 or above

⚠️ Signs:

🔹 Severe hypertension

🔹 Pounding headache

🔹 Flushing and sweating above the injury

🔹 Slow heart rate

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Sit upright, lower the legs

✅ Loosen tight clothing

✅ Check bladder: catheter kinked or full?

✅ Check bowel for impaction

🚑 Escalate: Notify the provider. Antihypertensives may be needed if BP stays high.

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Sit up, then find the trigger: bladder, bowel, skin!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Neuro #SpinalCordInjury #AutonomicDysreflexia #CriticalCare #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: A client's ABG results are pH 7.30, PaCO2 52 mmHg and HCO3 25 mEq/L. How should the nurse interpret these results?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #248!

🫁 pH 7.30 and PaCO2 52. Can you interpret this ABG in 10 seconds?

This is a HIGH-YIELD ABG question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: C — Respiratory Acidosis

🧠 Rationale: The pH is below 7.35, so this is acidosis.

The PaCO2 is high (above 45), which matches the acidosis, so the cause is respiratory.

The HCO3 is normal, so the kidneys have not compensated yet.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: ABG Interpretation

📊 Normal Values:

🔹 pH: 7.35 to 7.45

🔹 PaCO2: 35 to 45 mmHg

🔹 HCO3: 22 to 26 mEq/L

⚠️ Common Causes of Respiratory Acidosis:

🔹 COPD

🔹 Opioid or sedative oversedation

🔹 Hypoventilation

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Support breathing and airway

✅ Encourage cough and deep breathing

✅ Give oxygen as prescribed

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

ROME: Respiratory Opposite, Metabolic Equal!

photos.question: An Rh-negative client has just given birth to an Rh-positive newborn. Which action should the nurse anticipate?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #249!

🤰 Rh-negative mom, Rh-positive baby. What does the nurse give, and when?

This is a HIGH-YIELD maternity question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: A — Give Rho(D) Immune Globulin Within 72 Hours

🧠 Rationale: The mother can make antibodies against Rh-positive blood.

Those antibodies could harm a future Rh-positive baby.

Rho(D) immune globulin given within 72 hours after birth helps prevent this.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Rh Incompatibility

💉 Medication: Rho(D) immune globulin (RhoGAM)

📅 When It Is Given:

🔹 Around 28 weeks of pregnancy

🔹 Within 72 hours after birth of an Rh-positive baby

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Give IM to the mother, not the baby

✅ Confirm the mother is Rh negative

✅ Check that consent is signed

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Rh negative mom gets RhoGAM: 28 weeks and 72 hours!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Maternity #OBNursing #RhoGAM #MaternalHealth #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: A client with schizophrenia is starting clozapine. Which lab value is most important for the nurse to monitor?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #250!

🧠 Clozapine has one lab you can NEVER skip. Do you know which one?

This is a HIGH-YIELD mental health question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: A — Absolute Neutrophil Count

🧠 Rationale: Clozapine can cause severe neutropenia (agranulocytosis).

A low neutrophil count raises the risk of serious infection.

The ANC is checked before starting and regularly during treatment.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Clozapine

💊 Drug Class: Atypical antipsychotic

🧠 Primary Use: Schizophrenia that has not responded to other drugs

⚠️ Watch For:

🔹 Fever, sore throat or flu-like symptoms

🔹 Seizures

🔹 Myocarditis

🔹 Constipation and drooling

🚨 Patient Teaching:

✅ Report sore throat or fever right away

✅ Keep every lab appointment

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Clozapine = Count those neutrophils!

photos.question: The nurse is teaching the parents of a child with celiac disease. Which food is safe for the child?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #251!

🍞 Bread, soup, crackers or rice. Which one is safe for a child with celiac disease?

This is a HIGH-YIELD pediatrics question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: D — Plain Rice

🧠 Rationale: Celiac disease is an immune reaction to gluten.

Gluten is found in wheat, barley and rye.

Rice and corn are naturally gluten free.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Celiac Disease

🧬 What It Is: Gluten damages the lining of the small intestine

⚠️ Signs:

🔹 Diarrhea and bulky, foul-smelling stools

🔹 Poor weight gain

🔹 Abdominal swelling

🔹 Irritability

🚨 Patient Teaching:

✅ Lifelong gluten-free diet

✅ Read every food label

✅ Oats only if labeled gluten free

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Avoid BROW: Barley, Rye, Oats (unless gluten free), Wheat!
